jokes.punchline: Andy has a dead crow — previously purchased by Ron — and swears on it as one would swear on the Bible. The crow is being used as a sacred oath object
jokes.explanation: This is the payoff on Ron's inexplicable crow purchase. 'I swear on this dead crow' as a solemn oath is exceptional absurdist comedy. The callback elevates it — we laughed at Ron buying crows without explanation, and now Andy is using one as a religious artifact. The vow itself ('I will never cook for you') is a spectacularly unhelpful promise. Justifies 8.5+ comfortably — highly quotable, perfect absurdist escalation, and a satisfying callback payoff.

jokes.text: I love you.
jokes.setup: Andy swears on the dead crow that he will never cook for Chris
jokes.punchline: Chris immediately and sincerely responds 'I love you' — treating Andy's bizarre oath as a touching act of care
jokes.explanation: Chris's sincere 'I love you' in response to the dead crow oath is perfectly in character — he's so positive and emotionally available that Andy swearing never to cook for him reads as an act of love. Two words with perfect character integration.

jokes.text: I just wanted to make sure that there were no hard feelings after I forced you to break up with Tom.
jokes.setup: Chris approaches Leslie to check in
jokes.punchline: Chris frames himself as having 'forced' them to break up — treating Tom's fake-dating bit as a real relationship that required intervention, which is absurd given Tom's behavior was entirely performative
jokes.explanation: Chris's sincerity about having broken up a fake relationship is good character comedy. His complete obliviousness to the joke nature of the Tom/Leslie situation while also inadvertently setting up the Ben/Leslie irony is well-layered.

jokes.text: Because it's irrelevant. He oversees every department. It simply can't happen.
jokes.setup: Chris mentions Ben told him he might want to socialize with someone from the government — Leslie prompts for who, but Chris says he didn't ask
jokes.punchline: Chris's statement that it 'simply can't happen' is dramatic irony — we know it's Leslie, he's talking to Leslie, and it absolutely is going to happen. The episode is literally about them getting closer
jokes.explanation: The dramatic irony is rich here — Chris is telling Leslie why she and Ben can't be together while also being the person who will presumably have to deal with it when they inevitably get together. Earns rewatch bonus because the irony is richer on a second viewing.

jokes.text: This is literally the best thing I've ever eaten. Mmm. And it's so bad for me. I'm gonna have to jog while I digest this. Excuse me.
jokes.setup: Chris has conceded the cook-off and is eating Ron's hamburger
jokes.punchline: He announces that he will literally jog while digesting — and then apparently does exactly that
jokes.explanation: Chris jogging while digesting is perfectly in character. His inability to simply enjoy food without exercising simultaneously is a good running gag for his character. The 'Excuse me' as he presumably actually gets up and jogs away mid-conversation is the visual payoff.

jokes.text: Hey. Well, I think I'm allergic to chutney. / Also, what's chutney? / No clue.
jokes.setup: Ben approaches Leslie after the cook-off, mentioning he thinks he's allergic to something
jokes.punchline: He adds 'Also, what's chutney?' — having already identified a potential chutney allergy before knowing what chutney is. Leslie's 'No clue' shows she also has no idea
jokes.explanation: The structure is excellent: having an allergic reaction to something before knowing what it is is perfect. Ben and Leslie's mutual ignorance ('No clue') bonds them through shared cluelessness and is endearing. Good character moment that also advances their relationship while being funny.

jokes.text: Do you know that wildflower mural up on the second floor? Yeah? You wanna meet there? Yeah. Okay.
jokes.setup: Ben suggests they find somewhere to talk about health initiative ideas; he naturally references the wildflower mural
jokes.punchline: Ben independently suggests the exact place Leslie described as her favorite place in the world — the bench in front of the mural — without knowing she named it as her favorite spot on her dating profile
jokes.explanation: This is an earned callback that doubles as a sweet romantic moment. Earlier, Leslie's insistence that the mural bench was her favorite place in the world (over Paris, Hawaii, the Grand Canyon) was played for laughs. Now Ben — without knowing — suggests meeting exactly there. The callback validates Leslie's love for the mural while also being genuinely sweet. Earns 8+ for the callback structure and the way it recontextualizes both jokes.

jokes.text: I don't know if the online thing is for me. I prefer to meet people in person. It's like door number two on Let's Make a Deal. Do you want the thing that you have, that you know you like, but isn't perfect, or do you give it up for what's behind door number two?
jokes.setup: Leslie reflects on the online dating experience
jokes.punchline: The 'Let's Make a Deal' metaphor is deployed earnestly and at length — Leslie is giving an elaborate game show metaphor about a simple dating choice
jokes.explanation: The metaphor is slightly overextended. The idea is fine but runs a bit long for the payoff. More functional than inspired.

jokes.text: I think I like what I have. I'm gonna try to make it work with Tom. / I'm kidding!
jokes.setup: Leslie concludes her 'Let's Make a Deal' reflection by apparently deciding to pursue Tom
jokes.punchline: Immediate self-reversal — 'I'm kidding!' — suggesting she let the premise run a beat and then had to abandon it
jokes.explanation: Quick self-correction joke. Gets a mild laugh from the misdirection but isn't particularly crafted.

jokes.text: I made 26 profiles, each designed to attract a different type of girl. Tom A. Haverford. Sporty and sexy. Tom B. Haverford, smooth and soulful. Which letter did you get? / N, Tom N. Haverford. / The N stands for nerd! I never even check that one, 'cause no one ever responds to it.
jokes.setup: Leslie asks Tom to be honest about how they got matched
jokes.punchline: Tom has created 26 dating profiles covering every letter of the alphabet. Leslie matched with Tom N, the nerd profile, which Tom has never gotten a response on. The N stands for nerd.
jokes.explanation: This is the episode's second standout joke and a perfect end to the Tom/Leslie arc. The revelation of 26 profiles is already funny (the scope of Tom's romantic scheming is absurd), then the alphabetical branding (Tom A. through Tom Z.) is inspired, and Leslie getting Tom N — the nerd, the one nobody responds to — is the perfect comedic comeuppance. 'The N stands for nerd!' delivered with mortification is excellent. Justifies 9+ because the concept (26 alphabetically organized dating personas) is genuinely original, the execution is tight, and the payoff (nerd profile, no responses) works on multiple levels simultaneously. Approaches the calibration anchor level.

jokes.text: Tom N. Haverford collects globes. / Great. That's enough. / His favorite movie is books.
jokes.setup: Tom continues to describe his nerd persona; Leslie tries to stop him
jokes.punchline: 'His favorite movie is books.' — after Leslie says 'That's enough,' Tom delivers this anyway. 'Favorite movie is books' is a deliberately dorky non-answer that conflates two different media
jokes.explanation: This is the episode's most quotable single line. 'His favorite movie is books' is perfect because: (1) it conflates movies and books, which is itself the joke — the nerd can't keep his media straight; (2) it's delivered against Leslie's 'That's enough,' proving Tom can't resist; (3) the concept is 100% original and immediately quotable. This is calibration-anchor territory. Easily justifies 8.5+ and may be the single best joke in the episode for sheer originality and quotability. 'Favorite movie is books' works as a complete joke in five words.

jokes.text: Donna? / Every time I want you to shut up, from now on. [Donna appears/does something]
jokes.setup: Tom is still going with the Tom N. Haverford details after being told to stop; Leslie looks for help
jokes.punchline: Leslie has apparently summoned Donna with a signal — 'Donna?' — and Donna appears to shut Tom up, suggesting Leslie has an arrangement with Donna for exactly this purpose
jokes.explanation: Leslie having Donna on standby to shut Tom up is a charming bit. 'Every time I want you to shut up, from now on' as the explanation reveals this is a new protocol being established in real time. Good character beat for both Leslie and Donna.

tmdb_overview: Leslie tries an online dating service, but doesn't end up with a stranger as she expects. Also, Chris challenges Ron to a grilling competition as part of his plans to make Pawnee healthier.
insight: Deadpan delivery carries a middling episode through 65 scattered jokes in 22 minutes.
